notes: Expectations reference the numbered non-negotiable rules in cli-audit-data/SKILL.md. The fixture does not name its own defects, so a run has to derive them. reserve_seat is the core case: a read-decide-write with no transaction and no locking, which is exactly the two-concurrent-actors analysis rule 4 demands.
expected_behavior: Rule 4 and 8: identifies reserve_seat as a read -> decide -> write executed outside any transaction, and walks through two concurrent callers that both observe seat_taken == false and both insert, double-booking the seat
Recommends a durable PostgreSQL guarantee for seat uniqueness, a UNIQUE constraint or INSERT ... ON CONFLICT, rather than relying on the Rust-side EXISTS check
Rule 3: states explicitly that the application-level check is not an integrity guarantee
Rule 9: flags the reqwest call to payments.example.com as an external network call made while deciding on durable state
Rule 10: flags that cancel() discards rows_affected(), so cancelling a non-existent reservation reports success
Rule 5: flags refund() as retryable with no idempotency protocol, so a retry after timeout credits the user twice
Produces an audit only. The fixture file is left unmodified
must_not: Editing or repairing the fixture: audit skills report, they do not fix
Accepting the Rust-side EXISTS check as sufficient protection for the seat invariant
Proposing SQLite or a mock as proof of the concurrency behaviour, which rule 13 forbids
Describing the race with hedged language such as 'unlikely' or 'normally', which the skill rejects in favour of falsifiable statements
